Initial triage (quick hits):
- No model rollouts in the 3h window. No config changes flagged in infra.
- Grafana trace shows a large cluster of requests with KV-cache miss count up 3x at ~16:28 — suggests cache churn around a high-cardinality prompt pattern.
- Routing: 95% of SL traffic was on r4-hosted-1 pool; that pool reported CPU saturation on offloading tasks at the same time.

Attached: trace and a compressed tail log. Proposed immediate steps:
1) Temporarily route a small percentage (~20%) of ShopLattice traffic to r4-hosted-2 (different host kernel) to see if tail improves.
2) Toggle prefix-KV caching to 'aggressive' for SL to reduce repeated generation cost.
3) If routing + cache mitigates, schedule a post-mortem and long-term fix (cache eviction tuning + routing policy changes).

Attachments: [trace-20261011-18z.log (LOG, 220 KB)]

- Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: David Kim <david@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Myers <jordan@shoplattice.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 18:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Slow SSE responses — huge tail p99 starting ~16:30 PT

Action taken at 18:00 PT:
- Flipped 20% of SL traffic to r4-hosted-2 as a canary. Observed immediate p99 drop on the canary from ~14s -> 1.1s. Bulk remained degraded.
- Enabled 'aggressive' prefix-KV caching for SL (hotfix flag). On metrics: backend tokens per request dropped ~22% on canary, and overall p99 for the routed subset improved.

Next steps (in-flight):
- Gradual ramp of traffic to r4-hosted-2 while monitoring latency and error rates.
- Prepare an emergency scaling plan: spin up 4 extra nodes in r4-hosted-1 if we see <10% improvement after 30m of routing adjustment.

I've attached the request sample we used and the dashboard screenshot.

-David

Subject: EXTERNAL — Exec sync: ShopLattice SSE tail-p99 regression (summary + next steps)

Marcus — quick summary and ask for exec visibility. Looping you in because this has surfaced across evening peak and ShopLattice is evaluating temporary fallbacks.

What happened (summary):
- 16:28 PT 2026-10-11: observed abrupt p99 tail increase for ShopLattice SSE traffic (from ~0.9s -> 12–18s). Affected ~18% of sessions during 16:20–18:50 PT.
- Root cause (early): high KV-cache miss rate coinciding with a traffic pattern of many unique long system messages; r4-hosted-1 nodes were showing CPU offload saturation. No model or config rollouts detected in the window.

Mitigation performed:
- 18:00 PT: 20% traffic routed to r4-hosted-2 (immediate p99 improvement on canary).
- 18:05 PT: aggressive prefix-KV caching enabled for ShopLattice; canary tokens per request fell ~22%.
- 18:10–18:40 PT: gradual ramp of traffic to r4-hosted-2; monitoring for regressions. No user-facing data loss; transient latency impact only.

Current status:
- Customer reports canary latency acceptable; we are ramping to 60% and watching p95/p99 closely.
- SRE recommends spinning +4 nodes in r4-hosted-1 as contingency if sustained p99 remains >2s after full ramp.

Customer impact and ask:
- We should provide ShopLattice a timeline for full remediation (root-cause fix + configuration safeguards). Suggested short timeline:
  * Immediate: complete ramp to 60% by 11:00 PT and continue monitoring (in progress).
  * 0–24h: backfill r4-hosted-1 capacity + tune cache eviction thresholds (SRE).
  * 24–72h: post-mortem and long-term routing policy updates + customer-safe defaults.

Requested support:
- Exec visibility and sign-off to start emergency capacity (spin up +4 r4-hosted-1 nodes) if SRE triggers after 30m.
- Approval to issue a short customer-facing incident note to ShopLattice later today (CS/Comms to own wording).

I've attached the perf screenshot and the trace we used. I'll stay on the thread for updates; Karthik and David will continue tech lead.

Thanks,
Sooj
